about.tool: A flexible pointed nib, usually in an oblique holder.
about.features: Shaded downstrokes, hairline upstrokes, ovals and loops; every thick and thin comes from pressure. Capitals 2.5 x-heights tall, as on the exemplar; the exemplar has no figures, so these are in the copybook style. An accent would leave the page above a capital, so the accented capitals are left out.
about.history: The English Roundhand of the writing masters, late 17th and 18th centuries; named after the engraved copper plates of their copybooks.
